terms.definition: A circuit where all components share one single loop.
terms.whyItMatters: Sets the rules: one current, shared volts, one break stops all.
terms.whereItIs: The chain of bulbs on one ribbon.

terms.definition: The identical amperes flowing through every series element.
terms.whyItMatters: One number describes the whole loop's flow.
terms.whereItIs: The meter reading the same at every bulb.

terms.definition: The supply volts dividing up across the series components.
terms.whyItMatters: It's why each equal bulb runs dimmer in series.
terms.whereItIs: The volt labels shrinking along the chain.

terms.definition: The rule that opening any point of a series loop kills its entire flow.
terms.whyItMatters: It explains string-light failures and why houses aren't series.
terms.whereItIs: The 'pop a bulb' instant darkness demo.
